question: How did Meta Platforms' accounting policy for recognizing credit losses on available-for-sale debt securities change between its fiscal year 2019 and fiscal year 2023 10-K filings?
answer: In its fiscal year 2019 10-K, Meta indicated that unrealized losses were charged against interest and other income, net, only when a decline in fair value was determined to be other-than-temporary, and noted that no such impairment charges had been recorded. In its fiscal year 2023 10-K, the policy evolved to align with newer accounting standards, where allowance for credit losses on AFS debt securities are recognized as a charge in interest and other income (expense), net, based on an assessment of expected credit losses, with any remaining unrealized losses included in accumulated other comprehensive income.
key_points: The 2019 policy required an 'other-than-temporary' impairment determination before charging losses to income.
The 2023 policy recognizes allowances for expected credit losses directly in interest and other income.
The 2023 policy separates credit losses (P&L) from remaining unrealized losses (Equity/AOCI).
